1. Load Libraries and Data

# Load our libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(tmap)
# Download NC counties Demographic data
ncCounties <- read_sf("https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=1Ks38Gmdlp58GBhOgb6FBmx8tIAfu0QDw")
# Change the map to the NC State Plane Projection
ncCountiesProj <- st_transform(ncCounties, "EPSG:32119")
st_crs(ncCountiesProj)
## Coordinate Reference System:
##   User input: EPSG:32119 
##   wkt:
## PROJCRS["NAD83 / North Carolina",
##     BASEGEOGCRS["NAD83",
##         DATUM["North American Datum 1983",
##             ELLIPSOID["GRS 1980",6378137,298.257222101,
##                 LENGTHUNIT["metre",1]]],
##         PRIMEM["Greenwich",0,
##             ANGLEUNIT["degree",0.0174532925199433]],
##         ID["EPSG",4269]],
##     CONVERSION["SPCS83 North Carolina zone (meter)",
##         METHOD["Lambert Conic Conformal (2SP)",
##             ID["EPSG",9802]],
##         PARAMETER["Latitude of false origin",33.75,
##             ANGLEUNIT["degree",0.0174532925199433],
##             ID["EPSG",8821]],
##         PARAMETER["Longitude of false origin",-79,
##             ANGLEUNIT["degree",0.0174532925199433],
##             ID["EPSG",8822]],
##         PARAMETER["Latitude of 1st standard parallel",36.1666666666667,
##             ANGLEUNIT["degree",0.0174532925199433],
##             ID["EPSG",8823]],
##         PARAMETER["Latitude of 2nd standard parallel",34.3333333333333,
##             ANGLEUNIT["degree",0.0174532925199433],
##             ID["EPSG",8824]],
##         PARAMETER["Easting at false origin",609601.22,
##             LENGTHUNIT["metre",1],
##             ID["EPSG",8826]],
##         PARAMETER["Northing at false origin",0,
##             LENGTHUNIT["metre",1],
##             ID["EPSG",8827]]],
##     CS[Cartesian,2],
##         AXIS["easting (X)",east,
##             ORDER[1],
##             LENGTHUNIT["metre",1]],
##         AXIS["northing (Y)",north,
##             ORDER[2],
##             LENGTHUNIT["metre",1]],
##     USAGE[
##         SCOPE["Engineering survey, topographic mapping."],
##         AREA["United States (USA) - North Carolina - counties of Alamance; Alexander; Alleghany; Anson; Ashe; Avery; Beaufort; Bertie; Bladen; Brunswick; Buncombe; Burke; Cabarrus; Caldwell; Camden; Carteret; Caswell; Catawba; Chatham; Cherokee; Chowan; Clay; Cleveland; Columbus; Craven; Cumberland; Currituck; Dare; Davidson; Davie; Duplin; Durham; Edgecombe; Forsyth; Franklin; Gaston; Gates; Graham; Granville; Greene; Guilford; Halifax; Harnett; Haywood; Henderson; Hertford; Hoke; Hyde; Iredell; Jackson; Johnston; Jones; Lee; Lenoir; Lincoln; Macon; Madison; Martin; McDowell; Mecklenburg; Mitchell; Montgomery; Moore; Nash; New Hanover; Northampton; Onslow; Orange; Pamlico; Pasquotank; Pender; Perquimans; Person; Pitt; Polk; Randolph; Richmond; Robeson; Rockingham; Rowan; Rutherford; Sampson; Scotland; Stanly; Stokes; Surry; Swain; Transylvania; Tyrrell; Union; Vance; Wake; Warren; Washington; Watauga; Wayne; Wilkes; Wilson; Yadkin; Yancey."],
##         BBOX[33.83,-84.33,36.59,-75.38]],
##     ID["EPSG",32119]]

2. Practice Maps

ncCounties|>
  tm_shape() +
  tm_polygons("popE")

pop2020 <- ncCountiesProj |>
  select(popE, geometry)|>
  # Area for each county
  mutate(area=st_area(ncCountiesProj))|>
  # Calculate population density
  mutate(pop.dens=units::set_units(popE/area,"1/km^2"))
pop2020 |>
  tm_shape()+
  tm_polygons("pop.dens")

# Population density map with equal intervals
equal.pop <- pop2020 |> # Map as an object called equal.pop
  tm_shape()+
  tm_polygons(fill = "pop.dens",
              # Use a blue color palette and equal interval scale
              fill.scale=tm_scale_intervals(style = "equal", values = "brewer.blues"),
              # Create a legend
              fill.legend = tm_legend(title=paste("North Carolina\n", "Population Density 2020\n", "\n(persons/sq. km)\n","(Equal Interval)\n"), 
                                      position = tm_pos_out("right","center"),frame=FALSE))+
  # Remove Frame From Map
  tm_layout(frame = FALSE,
            outer.margins = 0)
# Print the map
equal.pop
## [plot mode] fit legend/component: Some legend items or map compoments do not
## fit well, and are therefore rescaled.
## ℹ Set the tmap option `component.autoscale = FALSE` to disable rescaling.

# Population density map with quantile intervals
quantile.pop <- pop2020 |> # Map as an object called quantile.pop
  tm_shape()+
  tm_polygons(fill = "pop.dens",
              # Use a purple color palette and quantile scale
              fill.scale=tm_scale_intervals(style = "quantile", values = "brewer.purples"),
              # Create a legend
              fill.legend = tm_legend(title=paste("North Carolina\n", "Population Density 2020\n", "\n(persons/sq. km)\n","(Quantile)\n"), 
                                      position = tm_pos_out("right","center"),frame=FALSE))+
  # Remove Frame From Map
  tm_layout(frame = FALSE,
            outer.margins = 0)
# Print the map
quantile.pop

  # Remove Frame From Map
  tm_layout(frame = FALSE,
            outer.margins = 0)
# Print the map
jenks.pop

## fit well, and are therefore rescaled.
## ℹ Set the tmap option `component.autoscale = FALSE` to disable rescaling.

# Population density map with tmap default (pretty)
pretty.pop <- pop2020 |> # Map as an object called pretty.pop
  tm_shape()+
  tm_polygons(fill = "pop.dens",
              # Use a red color palette and pretty scale
              fill.scale=tm_scale_intervals(style = "pretty", values = "brewer.reds"),
              # Create a legend
              fill.legend = tm_legend(title=paste("North Carolina\n", "Population Density 2020\n", "\n(persons/sq. km)\n","(Pretty)\n"), 
                                      position = tm_pos_out("right","center"),frame=FALSE))+
  # Remove Frame From Map
  tm_layout(frame = FALSE,
            outer.margins = 0)
# Print the map
pretty.pop

tmap_arrange(pretty.pop,equal.pop,jenks.pop,quantile.pop)

  tm_shape() +
  tm_polygons(fill="percent.female",
              title="% Female\n2020 Census",
              values="pu_gn_div",

              style="equal") +

            outer.margins=0,
            legend.position = tm_pos_out("right", "center"),

            title.position = tm_pos_out("center", "top")
  ) +
  tm_credits("Arnav Pandey, September 2026\nData: 2020 US Census\nGEOG 215",
             position = tm_pos_in("left", "bottom")

3. My Map

Section 1: Public Transit Map

# Map of public transit usage
publicTransit <- ncCountiesProj|>
  select(popE, public.transportationE)|>
  mutate(percent.pubTransitUse = public.transportationE/popE*100)

PubTransitMap <- publicTransit |>
  tm_shape()+
  tm_bubbles(size="percent.pubTransitUse",
    fill = "green",
    size.legend = tm_legend("% Public Transit Use")
  )+
  tm_layout(frame=FALSE, 
            legend.frame=TRUE,
            legend.position = tm_pos_out("right", "bottom"))
PubTransitMap

Section 2: Median Income Map
